purpose: Bounded Fair Work Commission case ledger preserving employer shutdown, unpaid promised entitlements, documented family and financial stress, lower-paid alternative employment, and a compensation order without treating the order as payment receipt or durable recovery.

events.geography: Victoria, Australia; Adam Smith v Adcon Admin Pty Ltd, U2024/1618
events.date_precision: termination date; decision issued 2024-10-04; alternative employment began 2024-03-01; employer wound up 2024-03-31
events.denominator: One publicly identified adjudicated employment case; no population denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from the primary Fair Work Commission decision [2024] FWC 2775
events.missingness: Worker payment instrument, compensation-order receipt, exact alternative-job conditions beyond reduced pay, later job duration, household recovery, trust, recurrence, and exit are not retained
events.exposure: Adcon told the worker it would stop operating, terminated him without the promised notice or redundancy payments, and entered court-appointed liquidation; unused leave was paid but notice and redundancy entitlements were not
events.alternatives_before_action: The worker made efforts to find work and secured continuing alternative employment beginning 2024-03-01 at a reduced rate; the public decision does not enumerate the full offer set, search cost, or non-use alternatives
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: The decision records financial stress and family pressure from job loss and unpaid entitlements; the alternative job produced $9,584 during the period used in the compensation calculation against $24,230.81 expected remuneration
events.choice_or_response: The worker contacted affected Workcover claimants, pursued an unfair-dismissal application, searched for work, and accepted lower-paid employment; the record does not measure whether acceptance was freely chosen under feasible alternatives
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Adcon controlled termination and promised entitlements; the worker controlled job search and legal challenge; the Commission controlled remedy; liquidation constrained practical enforcement
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: The Commission found the dismissal unfair, rejected reinstatement because the employer had wound up, and ordered $17,531.43 gross plus superannuation within 14 days; the order was increased for unpaid notice and redundancy entitlements
events.immediate_outcome: A same-case lower-paid alternative job, quantified earnings trade-off, reported family/financial burden, employer liquidation, and formal compensation order are observed or reported; compensation receipt is not
events.protected_outcome: The worker obtained continuing alternative employment and earned $9,584 during the relevant counterfactual period; some leave entitlements were paid
events.sacrificed_outcome: The original job ended, notice and redundancy payments were initially unpaid, replacement earnings were lower, and household stress was reported; longer-term recovery is unknown
events.cost_risk_transfer: The worker carried search, income-gap, and enforcement risk while employer insolvency reduced the practical value of formal remedies; the Commission recognized the residual loss in the order
events.later_outcome: Alternative employment, reported stress, and formal compensation are visible, but order receipt, job durability, household recovery, trust, recurrence, switching, and exit remain unknown
events.meaning_and_attribution: The worker attributed financial stress and family pressure to job loss and unpaid entitlements; this is a case-level meaning signal, not a standardized trust measure
events.public_or_collective_response: Individual Commission action and communication with affected Workcover claimants are observed; no later collective or political action is reported
events.counterexample: A lower-paid replacement job and partial final-pay receipt can coexist with unpaid entitlements, employer liquidation, family stress, and an unverified compensation order
events.source_and_uncertainty: Primary Fair Work Commission [2024] FWC 2775, https://www.fwc.gov.au/documents/decisionssigned/pdf/2024fwc2775.pdf; the decision accepts the worker's unchallenged evidence and orders compensation but does not confirm payment or later recovery

arrows.evidence: The decision records financial stress and family pressure after job loss and states that notice and redundancy entitlements were not paid, although unused leave was paid
arrows.counterexample: The case is one unchallenged claimant account, not a population estimate or causal household effect
arrows.remaining_gap: Household budget, duration, debt, care substitution, and independent corroboration

arrows.evidence: The worker secured continuing alternative employment beginning 2024-03-01 at a reduced rate and earned $9,584 during the relevant period
arrows.counterexample: A replacement job does not show the full offer set, reachability, equivalence, search cost, or voluntariness
arrows.remaining_gap: Applications, offers, hours, benefits, travel, job conditions, and later duration

arrows.to: assessed residual loss and compensation order
arrows.evidence: The Commission deducted $9,584 from $24,230.81 anticipated remuneration, then ordered $17,531.43 gross plus superannuation including an additional week for unpaid notice/redundancy effects
arrows.counterexample: A legal calculation is not a welfare-equivalent measure or proof that the order was paid
arrows.remaining_gap: Net amount, payment execution, receipt, and residual household loss

arrows.evidence: The employer wound up and entered court-appointed liquidation; the Commission found reinstatement inappropriate and ordered compensation instead
arrows.counterexample: A formal order can exist even when the original workplace no longer exists to restore
arrows.remaining_gap: Liquidator/FEG implementation, payment priority, and actual recovery

arrows.from: lower-paid alternative work and compensation order
arrows.to: durable recovery, trust, recurrence, or exit
arrows.evidence: The public decision ends at alternative employment, reported stress, liquidation, and the compensation order
arrows.counterexample: A worker can adapt and obtain an order while remaining financially exposed and unable to recover the original job
arrows.remaining_gap: Payment receipt, job duration, household recovery, trust, later work, recurrence, switching, and exit

boundary: This ledger adds one adjudicated employment-shutdown episode with reported household stress, lower-paid alternative employment, quantified earnings, liquidation, and a compensation order. It does not establish compensation receipt, FEG recovery, durable employment, household recovery, trust, recurrence, or exit.
storage_boundary: No claimant file, payment instrument, direct personal data beyond the public case reference, or bulk archive is retained; only bounded primary decision fields, dates, reported alternatives, money and household effects, remedy stages, uncertainty, and open downstream arrows are represented.
